group.passage: Last Sunday, a nature club led a walk along the wooden path beside the mangrove forest near MRT Hongshulin Station in Tamsui. After the walk, eight people who joined it left comments on the club’s web page.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: Amy
passage_parts.text: I loved the “water pens”! Our guide showed us long green seedlings that hang from the branches like pens. They begin to grow while they are still on the tree. When they are ready, they drop into the mud below.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Ben
passage_parts.text: We came at high tide, so the mud was under water, and only the tops of the trees stood above it. I didn’t see a single crab. Next time, I’ll look up the tide times before I go.

passage_parts.label: C
passage_parts.title: Cindy
passage_parts.text: My son watched the fiddler crabs on the mud for twenty minutes. He had never seen so many of them in one place. Now he wants to come back with his camera next weekend.

passage_parts.label: D
passage_parts.title: David
passage_parts.text: My favorite part was the mudskippers. They are fish, but they hop around on the mud like little frogs. I didn’t know that a fish could spend so much time out of the water!

passage_parts.label: E
passage_parts.title: Emma
passage_parts.text: Honestly, I was a little bored. It was hot, the path was crowded, and the mud did not smell good. Next time, I think I’d rather spend the day at the beach.

passage_parts.label: F
passage_parts.title: Frank
passage_parts.text: I didn’t know this area has been a nature reserve since 1986. Visitors are not allowed to walk into the forest itself, so we stayed on the wooden path the whole time.

passage_parts.label: G
passage_parts.title: Grace
passage_parts.text: Bring something to help you see birds far away! I saw white egrets walking slowly through the mud, looking for food. Our guide said that many other birds come here every winter.

passage_parts.label: H
passage_parts.title: Henry
passage_parts.text: The guide explained that these trees can live in salty water, which most plants can’t do. Their roots spread wide in the soft mud and help hold the trees in place.

evidence: My son watched the fiddler crabs on the mud for twenty minutes.

2.explanation_zh: Amy 說導覽員給大家看長長的綠色小苗 that hang from the branches like pens（像筆一樣掛在樹枝上），這也是這種樹叫「水筆仔」（water pens）的原因。look like 後面接複數名詞 pens，照抄即可。

回到 Amy 的留言：掛在樹枝上的綠色小苗看起來像什麼？

3.explanation_zh: 正確的是 A、E、F。A：Amy 說小苗還在樹上時就開始生長（They begin to grow while they are still on the tree）。E：Frank 說遊客不准走進樹林，所以全程都待在木棧道上。F：Henry 說這些樹能活在鹹水裡。B 只看 Ben 的留言好像成立，但他說的是漲潮時，而 Cindy、David、Grace 都在泥灘上看到動物；C 只看 Cindy 的留言好像成立，但 Ben 漲潮時一隻螃蟹也沒看到；D 留言都沒有提到租船。
evidence: They begin to grow while they are still on the tree.
Visitors are not allowed to walk into the forest itself, so we stayed on the wooden path the whole time.

option_notes_zh.B: 和明文矛盾：Ben 說的是漲潮（high tide）時泥灘在水下；Cindy、David 都看到動物在泥灘上活動，可見退潮時泥灘會露出來，不是整天泡在水裡。

option_notes_zh.D: 八則留言都沒有提到租船遊覽；Frank 甚至說遊客不能走進樹林，只能待在木棧道上。

3.strategy_zh: 跨留言判斷：每個選項先找出相關的留言，再看有沒有其他留言補充或推翻；只看一則留言就下結論，容易選到 B、C。
hints: 每個選項都要找到明寫的留言，還要看其他留言有沒有說相反的情況。

translation_zh.text:
【引言】上星期天，一個自然社團帶大家沿著淡水捷運紅樹林站附近、紅樹林旁的木棧道散步。活動結束後，八位參加的人在社團網頁上留言。
【A Amy】我好喜歡「水筆仔」！導覽員給我們看長長的綠色小苗，像一支支筆掛在樹枝上。它們還在樹上時就開始生長，等準備好了，就掉進下面的泥巴裡。
【B Ben】我們是漲潮時來的，所以泥灘都在水底下，只有樹梢露出水面。我連一隻螃蟹都沒看到。下次我出發前會先查好潮汐時間。
【C Cindy】我兒子在泥灘上看招潮蟹看了二十分鐘。他從來沒在同一個地方看過這麼多招潮蟹。現在他說下週末要帶相機再來。
【D David】我最喜歡的是彈塗魚。牠們是魚，卻像小青蛙一樣在泥巴上跳來跳去。我以前都不知道魚可以離開水這麼久！
【E Emma】老實說，我覺得有點無聊。天氣很熱，步道很擁擠，泥巴的味道也不好聞。下次我寧可去海邊玩一天。
【F Frank】我之前不知道這裡從 1986 年起就是自然保留區。遊客不准走進樹林裡，所以我們全程都待在木棧道上。
【G Grace】記得帶能看遠處鳥兒的東西！我看到白色的白鷺在泥灘上慢慢走著找食物。導覽員說，每年冬天還有很多其他的鳥會來這裡。
【H Henry】導覽員解釋，這些樹能活在鹹水裡，這是大多數植物辦不到的。它們的根在柔軟的泥巴裡向四周伸展，幫忙把樹固定住。

status_reason: 人工審核（第 1 輪判定）：record_verification 判 verified（程式、兩位盲解、稽核、事實核對都通過），判定改為退回，原因在選文本身，不能只改註解。(1) 選文內部矛盾：引言說 eight people who joined it（八人參加同一場導覽）留言，Ben 卻說 We came at high tide, so the mud was under water, and only the tops of the trees stood above it. I didn’t see a single crab.，同一場導覽中 Cindy 的兒子 watched the fiddler crabs on the mud for twenty minutes、David 看彈塗魚 hop around on the mud、Grace 看白鷺 walking slowly through the mud，泥灘不可能同時淹在水下又露出來；Ben 的 Next time, I’ll look up the tide times before I go 也和「社團排定的導覽」不合。(2) 第 3 題兩個誘答的判定正依賴這組矛盾：解析要 Ben「漲潮時來」才能推翻 C（任何時間都看得到螃蟹），又要其他人「同時」在泥灘上看到動物才能推翻 B（泥灘整天泡在水裡），細心的考生會被「到底是不是同一場」卡住。重生建議：把引言改成不同日子的參觀留言（例如 visitors who went there last month left comments），或把 Ben 改成另一天自行前往（例如 I went back on Wednesday at high tide…），並同步改寫第 3 題 B、C 的解析；填充、簡答與其他四個選項可沿用。
